highlights: Review proposed file changes in the app: browse them, read feedback, edit comments, and ask the agent about specific changed lines.
A redesigned sidebar keeps tasks organized, lets you reorder pinned tasks, and helps you find tasks and project files faster.
Attach general files and images more easily, preview images and videos, and save unfinished prompts with their attachments for later.
New plugins connect to UC San Diego Kuali Build and n8n, using your own sign-in or API key and only the permissions you authorize.
Opt-in computer use lets the app work on your desktop with visible setup and activity, and updates install more reliably.
You can now download and install app updates from inside the app, with progress, release notes, and an automatic restart.
Each model now uses the correct account key, and you can replace or remove keys without restarting the app.
Signing in to add-ons such as GitHub, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365 is easier and more flexible.
When the app asks you to approve work, you now see complete details, including full proposed file changes.
Many small fixes make the app more stable and polished, including a refreshed look and better voice input on Mac.
Memory now turns on by default, fills in the previous seven days of summaries, and can optionally sync your notes between computers through OneDrive.
Cloud models were refreshed to include GPT-6.1 Sol, and Flash is now the default model for new chats.
The managed Codex engine now updates itself automatically after startup when no Codex session is running, and handles an already-updated shared runtime more clearly.
Threads now use Done and Reopen wording, with a cleaner sidebar and buttons that open your memory and log folders.
On Windows, computer use no longer opens an extra console window, and the installer version is now shown in Diagnostics.

setup: Update the Harness app from Settings > About > Check for Updates. A Harness update also brings UCSD-managed configuration and built-in skills.
To see which installer was used on your desktop, check Settings > General > Diagnostics. It is diagnostic only; Harness does not check for newer installers.
faq: Computer use is off by default. To opt in, open Settings > General and turn on Computer use; turning it off again removes the computer-use tools after a restart.
Permission modes are set per conversation from the composer. Changing the mode in one conversation does not change any other conversation.
privacy: Memory notes are kept in a local folder on each computer. Optional OneDrive sync, turned on in Settings > General > Memory, copies them to your OneDrive so every computer sees the same notes.
Usage analytics use a random installation ID. Events exclude conversation and file content, identifying workspace details, model names and authentication tokens.
skills: To share a skill you created, find it under Your Skills and select Share with UCSD. The confirmation names the exact local folder and explains which files will become public.
citizen: Use Supervised mode the first time you run an unfamiliar task, so commands needing additional permissions and file changes wait for your approval.
When giving the agent a task, you can add files, quote a previous response, or include a skill so the agent has the context it needs.
models: Setup requires a Mac or Windows PC, a TritonAI API key, and an internet connection. The installer configures TritonAI access for you.
In Settings > Runtime, the Access key status shows only the last four characters of your key, so you can identify it without revealing the full key.
